deed: Sidney Farber develops chemotherapy against childhood leukemia and founds the Jimmy Fund
title: Sidney Farber gave children with leukemia their first remissions and founded the Jimmy Fund

trailer.text: Sidney Farber was a pathologist and a researcher of childhood cancer, and the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute is now named after him.
In those days, a diagnosis of leukemia in a child was considered a death sentence.
According to the Dana-Farber Institute, in 1947 Farber tried a drug called aminopterin on 16 seriously ill children, and 10 of them reached temporary remissions.
To fund the research, the Jimmy Fund was born, named after a sick child who appeared on a radio show in 1948.
According to a research article, today about 85% of children diagnosed with the once fatal disease are cured.

stations.title: Before: leukemia in a child was a verdict

paragraphs.text: According to the Dana-Farber Institute, since leukemia was first described in 1845 its prognosis had remained grim: death, sometimes painful, usually within weeks of diagnosis.
According to the Institute, apart from a brief respite with cortisone therapy, doctors had almost nothing to offer the sick children.
A review of more than 200 untreated cases of acute childhood leukemia from that period found a median survival of 3.9 months, from the first symptom to death.
At Memorial Hospital in New York, between 1926 and 1947, only 3 of 150 adults and children with acute leukemia survived a year.
Sidney Farber was born in 1903 in Buffalo, New York State, the third of 14 children.
In the mid-nineteen-forties, Farber was a pathologist at Boston's Children's Hospital.
His lab was in the basement of the building, and it was small, damp and poorly ventilated.

According to Blood Cancer UK, in 1947, moved and frustrated by the number of children dying of leukemia, Farber decided to move from post-mortem examinations to the study of chemicals and the treatment of patients.
Farber believed that a drug that would chemically block folic acid would stop the production of the abnormal bone marrow associated with leukemia.
Farber, Diamond and three research assistants gave folic acid to 90 patients with advanced cancer, including acute leukemia.
According to the American Society of Hematology, Farber tried folic acid in some children, but it failed and seemingly made them worse.
In 1947 the team began giving a drug called aminopterin to children seriously ill with leukemia.
One of them was an 8-year-old boy seriously ill with acute leukemia, who received the drug daily.
The team adjusted the daily dose within a range of 0.25 to 1.0 mg.
Of the 16 children, 10 had unprecedented remissions.
Farber and his team showed for the first time that it was possible to suppress the proliferation of malignant cells and to restore normal bone-marrow function in children with acute leukemia.
This was the first clinical remission with chemotherapy ever reported for childhood leukemia.
The researchers emphasized that the changes were temporary and were accompanied by serious drug-related side effects.

stations.title: The report: disbelief, then letters from across the country

paragraphs.text: Farber reported the results in the June 3, 1948, issue of the New England Journal of Medicine.
According to the Dana-Farber Institute, much of the scientific community reacted with a mixture of disbelief and resistance.
According to the Institute, such a discovery by a young pathologist in a basement lab, with little money, staff or equipment, was seen as presumptuous.
Calls, telegrams and letters came from doctors throughout New England, and later across the country, and Farber answered each one personally.
In a follow-up study of about 60 children, more than half of the patients experienced important remissions, with survival beyond expectation.
Dameshek's team at Tufts reported remissions in 10 of 32 leukemia patients treated with an antifolate.
According to Blood Cancer UK, Farber continued to see successful remissions, and more patients and families came to his clinic.

stations.title: Jimmy, a radio show and Fenway Park

paragraphs.text: The Variety Club of New England established the Children's Cancer Research Foundation and began funding Farber's small outpatient clinic.
Farber and Bill Koster of the club searched the hospital wards for a representative who could bring attention to fundraising for cancer research.
They found Einar Gustafson, a boy being treated for a rare form of lymphoma.
On May 22, 1948, Einar, a 12-year-old boy, appeared on the radio show Truth or Consequences.
To protect his privacy, Farber insisted that the boy be identified only as "Jimmy".
The show's host, Ralph Edwards, asked listeners to donate.
According to the Dana-Farber Institute, the foundation was renamed the Jimmy Fund.
The success of the Jimmy Fund led Farber to understand the importance of marketing in furthering scientific knowledge about diseases.
The Boston Braves baseball team chose the Jimmy Fund as the beneficiary of its community fundraising initiatives.
When the Braves moved to Milwaukee, the Boston Red Sox made the Fund their preferred charity.
In 1952 the four-story Jimmy Fund Building opened, at a cost of $1.47 million.
According to an article in PMC, Jimmy was diagnosed with Burkitt lymphoma, not leukemia, and he was cured.
According to Blood Cancer UK, he survived the cancer and lived to the age of 65.
In 1998 Einar Gustafson threw the ceremonial first pitch at a Red Sox–Yankees game at Fenway Park.

stations.title: Total care, and another childhood cancer

paragraphs.text: According to Healio and the Dana-Farber website, under the idea of "total care" Farber felt that all care for patients should be provided in one location.
In the mid-1950s Farber persuaded Children's Hospital to give him an entire inpatient floor on which to put his principles into practice.
According to one source, the model has since become the standard in pediatric cancer care worldwide.
In 1955 Farber discovered that actinomycin D and radiation could produce remission in Wilms' tumor, a pediatric cancer of the kidneys.
By the end of the century, the National Wilms Tumor Study Group had achieved a 90% survival rate in children with the tumor.
From the early 1950s until his death in 1973, Farber was a key presenter at Congressional hearings on cancer research budgets.
Between 1957 and 1967, the National Cancer Institute's budget jumped from $48 million to $176 million.
Farber's activity contributed to the creation of the Clinical Trials Cooperative Group Program and the Chemotherapy National Service Center within the National Cancer Institute.
According to Whonamedit, Congress appropriated $5 million to establish the Chemotherapy National Service Center.

stations.title: What remains: a drug, an institute, children who recover

paragraphs.text: According to Blood Cancer UK, aminopterin was later developed into methotrexate, which is less toxic and is commonly used in chemotherapy today.
Methotrexate, which has comparable effectiveness and fewer side effects, remains a standard component of the treatment of acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
In the early 1960s, median survival in acute leukemia was still under one year, and fewer than 1% of children survived free of the disease.
According to an article in PMC, since Farber's research, disease-free survival has risen from 0% to about 80%.
According to another article, today about 85% of children diagnosed with the disease are cured.
According to Mel Mann in OncoDaily, Farber did not cure childhood leukemia but proved that it could be treated.
According to him, the remissions were short and most children relapsed, but the proof was there that cancer could be treated with a drug.
In 1969 the Institute's charter was expanded to provide services to patients of all ages.
In 1974 the foundation was renamed the Sidney Farber Cancer Center, and in 1976 the Sidney Farber Cancer Institute.
In 1983, the long-term support of the Charles Dana Foundation was acknowledged in the Institute's present name, Dana-Farber.
The Jimmy Fund is the Institute's principal charity.
According to the Institute, Dana-Farber researchers contributed to the development of 35 of 75 cancer drugs recently approved by the FDA.
The Lasker Award was given to Farber for the original use of aminopterin and methotrexate in acute childhood leukemia and for his leadership in the search for chemical agents against cancer.
According to the Lasker Foundation, the award was given for turning the despair of physicians and scientists toward cancer into vigorous and productive research.
Farber also received the Gold-Headed Cane Award.
Over his career, Farber published more than 270 books and research articles.
In a 1971 article he said that anyone who predicts a date for discovery is no longer a scientist.
On March 30, 1973, Farber died of cardiac arrest while working in his office.
According to the authors of an article in PMC, Farber's contributions received less recognition than he deserved.

claims.text: לפי Blood Cancer UK, אמינופטרין פותח אחר כך למתוטרקסט, שהוא פחות רעיל ונפוץ כיום בכימותרפיה.
claims.quote: This was later developed to methotrexate which is less toxic and is commonly used today in chemotherapy treatment.

claims.text: מתוטרקסט, שיעילותו דומה אך תופעות הלוואי שלו פחותות מאלה של אמינופטרין, הוא עד היום רכיב סטנדרטי בטיפול בלוקמיה לימפובלסטית חריפה.
claims.quote: methotrexate, which has comparable effectiveness but fewer adverse effects than aminopterin, remains a standard component of the treatment of acute lymphoblastic leukemia

claims.text: בראשית שנות ה-60 ההישרדות החציונית בלוקמיה חריפה הייתה מתחת לשנה, ופחות מ-1% מהילדים שרדו ללא המחלה.
claims.quote: during the early 1960s, the median survival for acute leukemia was under one year, with fewer than 1% of children surviving without the illness.

claims.text: לפי מאמר ב-PMC, מאז המחקר של פרבר הישרדות ללא מחלה עלתה מ-0% לכ-80%.
claims.quote: the prevailing disease-free survival has risen from 0% to approximately 80%, marking a distinctive accomplishment

claims.text: לפי מל מאן ב-OncoDaily, פרבר לא ריפא לוקמיה בילדים אלא הוכיח שאפשר לטפל בה.
claims.quote: He did not cure childhood leukemia. He proved it could be treated.

claims.text: לפי מל מאן, ההפוגות היו קצרות ורוב הילדים חזרו לחלות, אך ההוכחה הייתה שאפשר לטפל בסרטן בתרופה.
claims.quote: The remissions were short. Most children relapsed. But the proof was there: cancer could be treated with a drug.

claims.text: ב-1969 הורחבה אמנת המכון כך שיעניק שירותים לחולים בכל גיל.
claims.quote: In 1969, the Institute's charter was expanded to provide services to patients of all ages.

claims.text: תמיכתה ארוכת הטווח של קרן צ'ארלס דנה הוכרה בשם המכון הנוכחי, דנה-פרבר, ב-1983.
claims.quote: The long-term support of the Charles A. Dana Foundation was acknowledged by incorporating the Institute under its present name in 1983.

claims.text: לפי המכון, חוקרי דנה-פרבר תרמו לפיתוח של 35 מתוך 75 תרופות לסרטן שאושרו לאחרונה על ידי ה-FDA.
claims.quote: Dana-Farber researchers have contributed to the development of 35 of 75 cancer drugs recently approved by the FDA for use in cancer patients.

claims.text: לפי קרן לאסקר, הפרס ניתן על הפיכת הייאוש של רופאים ומדענים כלפי סרטן למחקר נמרץ ופורה.
claims.quote: In recognition of his success in converting the early hopelessness and defeatism of physicians and medical scientists toward cancer into vigorous and productive research.

claims.text: לפי מאמר ב-PMC, פרבר קיבל את פרס Gold-Headed Cane ב-1972.
claims.quote: receiving the esteemed Gold-Headed Cane Award in 1972

claims.text: פרבר פרסם יותר מ-270 ספרים ומאמרי מחקר לאורך הקריירה שלו.
claims.quote: authored more than 270 influential books and research articles throughout his distinguished career

claims.text: פרבר אמר בכתבה מ-1971 שמי שחוזה תאריך לגילוי אינו עוד מדען.
claims.quote: Any man who predicts a date for discovery is no longer a scientist

claims.text: לפי מחברי מאמר ב-PMC, תרומותיו של פרבר זכו להכרה פחותה ממה שהגיע לו.
claims.quote: his monumental contributions to pediatric pathology and oncology have received relatively lesser recognition than he deserved.

claims.text: לפי מאמר ב-PMC, פרבר נולד ב-30 בספטמבר 1903 לסיימון ומטילדה פרבר.
claims.quote: Farber, born in Buffalo, New York, on September 30, 1903, to Simon and Matilda Farber

claims.text: לפי Healio, פרבר נולד ב-20 בספטמבר 1903 והיה השלישי מבין 14 ילדים.
claims.quote: Farber was born on Sept. 20, 1903, in Buffalo, N.Y., and was the third of 14 children.

claims.text: לפי מאמר ב-PMC, שישה מקרים לא הראו תגובה לטיפול וארבעה ילדים מתו מהמחלה.
claims.quote: Six cases demonstrated no response to the treatment, and four had passed away due to the illness.

claims.text: לפי אתר דנה-פרבר, ב-1947 פרבר ייסד את קרן המחקר לסרטן ילדים.
claims.quote: In 1947, Sidney Farber, MD, founded the Children's Cancer Research Foundation, dedicated to providing compassionate, state-of-the-art treatment to children with cancer

claims.text: לפי LITFL, ב-1948 נוסדה קרן המחקר לסרטן ילדים.
claims.quote: 1948 – Founded the Children's Cancer Research Foundation (CCRF)

claims.text: סידני פרבר היה פתולוג וחוקר סרטן ילדים, ועל שמו נקרא כיום מכון הסרטן דנה-פרבר.
claims.quote: The institute was formally rebranded as the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute (DFCI) in 1983.

claims.text: סידני פרבר היה פתולוג וחוקר סרטן ילדים, ועל שמו נקרא כיום מכון הסרטן דנה-פרבר.
claims.quote: In 1929, he became the first full-time pathologist at Children's Hospital.

claims.text: כדי לממן את המחקר נולדה קרן ג'ימי, שנקראה על שם ילד חולה שהופיע בתוכנית רדיו ב-1948.
claims.quote: In May 1948, at the CCRF, the renowned program on radio known as 'Truth or Consequences' featured 'Jimmy,' who was a cancer patient about 12 years of age.

claims.text: כדי לממן את המחקר נולדה קרן ג'ימי, שנקראה על שם ילד חולה שהופיע בתוכנית רדיו ב-1948.
claims.quote: which was renamed the Jimmy Fund.

claims.text: ב-22 במאי 1948 הופיע איינר, נער בן 12, בתוכנית הרדיו Truth or Consequences.
claims.quote: On May 22, 1948, radio star Ralph Edwards was to ask for donations on a broadcast of his radio show

claims.text: ב-22 במאי 1948 הופיע איינר, נער בן 12, בתוכנית הרדיו Truth or Consequences.
claims.quote: Einar Gustafson, a 12-year-old boy whom Dr. Farber had dubbed "Jimmy" to protect his privacy.

claims.text: הצלחת קרן ג'ימי הובילה את פרבר להבין את חשיבות השיווק בקידום הידע המדעי על מחלות.
claims.quote: Farber's realization of the marketing significance in furthering scientific understanding of diseases

claims.text: ב-1974 שונה שם הקרן למרכז הסרטן סידני פרבר, וב-1976 למכון הסרטן סידני פרבר.
claims.quote: The Children's Cancer Research Foundation is renamed the Sidney Farber Cancer Center in honor of its founder.

claims.text: ב-1974 שונה שם הקרן למרכז הסרטן סידני פרבר, וב-1976 למכון הסרטן סידני פרבר.
claims.quote: Two years later, the name is again modified, becoming the Sidney Farber Cancer Institute.

claims.text: פרבר קיבל גם את פרס Gold-Headed Cane.
claims.quote: 1972 Sidney Farber

claims.text: ב-30 במרץ 1973 מת פרבר מדום לב בעודו עובד במשרדו.
claims.quote: Regrettably, he succumbed to cardiac arrest while on duty on March 30, 1973

claims.text: ב-30 במרץ 1973 מת פרבר מדום לב בעודו עובד במשרדו.
claims.quote: He died while working in his office on March 30, 1973.

claims.text: לפי האגודה האמריקאית להמטולוגיה, פרבר ניסה חומצה פולית אצל כמה ילדים, אך היא נכשלה ונראה שאף החמירה את מצבם.
claims.quote: He tried it in some children, and it failed and seemingly made them worse.
